(5) Bare/unnamespaced ext key — SPEC §4.5.1 requires every immediate child of ext to be reverse-DNS namespaced. (6) An item without `hidden`: the owners' view always says whether the recipient hid the badge, so a hidden holder is never mistaken for one who shows

payload.invalid-examples.json of https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/registry/sync-jobs/retry/0.1: (1) Neither jobId nor allFailed. The oneOf makes the discriminator mandatory — an empty payload must not be readable as 'retry everything'. (2) Both jobId and allFailed. Ambiguous intent: a consumer would have to choose between one job and all of them, so the schema refuses rather than letting each implementation pick. (3) allFailed: false. The const pins it to true so the member means 'do the bulk operation' and never 'do something else'; a false here is a client that meant to send jobId. (4) Empty jobId. minLength 1 stops a dropped identifier arriving as a well-formed request naming nothing.

payload.invalid-examples.json of https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/rooms/community/create/0.1: (1) No visibility. The tier is fixed for the life of the room, so a community never chooses it on an administrator's behalf. (2) No reason. Creating a room the community owns is an act of the community, and the audit trail records why. (3) A room identifier supplied by the caller. The community's VTA mints the room's identity; an administrator naming one would be asking the community to own a DID whose key it does not hold. (4) Bare/unnamespaced ext key — SPEC §4.5.1 requires every immediate child of ext to be reverse-DNS namespaced.

payload.invalid-examples.json of https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/vetting/vetters/resend/0.1: (1) No `memberDid`. A resend always concerns the sender's own grant; naming a member would make this a way to push someone else's role credential around. (2) No `credentialId` selector. A member holds at most one live grant, and the community delivers that one. (3) No delivery address. The credential goes to the DID the grant names, never to one the request chooses. (4) No `validitySeconds`. A resend delivers the credential as issued; extending a grant is vtc/vetting/vetters/grant's business. (5) `ext` keys must be reverse-DNS namespaces (SPEC §4.5.1).
